node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Choose attribute to compare
node.description: Identify which measurable attribute is being compared, such as length, mass, capacity, area or duration.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare length directly
node.description: Compare the length, height or width of objects by aligning them and using comparison language.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare mass directly
node.description: Compare object mass by hefting or balance experiences and describe heavier, lighter or same mass.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare capacity directly
node.description: Compare container capacity by filling, pouring or direct matching experiences.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare duration directly
node.description: Compare durations using everyday events and language such as longer, shorter, earlier and later.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Iterate informal units
node.description: Measure by placing informal units end to end or repeatedly using one unit.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: No gaps or overlaps
node.description: Measure accurately by placing units with no gaps or overlaps along or over the attribute.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Same size units
node.description: Recognise that repeated units must be the same size to produce a meaningful measure.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Count units as measure
node.description: Use the count of equal units as the numerical measure of an attribute.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Choose informal unit
node.description: Choose an informal unit that suits the attribute and size of the object being measured.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Select length units
node.description: Select appropriate metric units for measuring length, distance, height or width.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Select mass units
node.description: Select appropriate metric units for measuring mass in everyday contexts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Select capacity units
node.description: Select appropriate metric units for measuring capacity or liquid volume.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Select time units
node.description: Select appropriate units for measuring duration such as seconds, minutes, hours, days and weeks.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Square units for area
node.description: Use square units to measure how much surface a flat region covers.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Estimate with metric units
node.description: Estimate measures using familiar benchmarks for common metric units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Metric prefixes and base units
node.description: Relate common metric prefixes and base units such as milli, centi, kilo, metre, gram and litre.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Convert length units
node.description: Convert between related metric length units such as millimetres, centimetres, metres and kilometres.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Convert mass and capacity units
node.description: Convert between related metric units for mass and capacity, such as grams, kilograms, millilitres and litres.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Convert area units
node.description: Convert between related square units while accounting for two-dimensional scaling.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conversion reasonableness
node.description: Check whether converted measurements are reasonable given the relative sizes of units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Measurement needs attribute focus
node.description: A measurement comparison must focus on a single attribute such as length, mass, capacity or duration.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Direct comparison needs alignment
node.description: For length comparison, objects should be aligned at a common starting point.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Equal units are needed
node.description: Measurement units must be equal-sized for a count of units to be meaningful.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit iteration counts repeats
node.description: Repeatedly placing the same unit measures how many unit lengths, areas or quantities fit the attribute.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Measurement is number and unit
node.description: A complete measurement includes both a number and a unit.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Smaller units give larger counts
node.description: For the same object, using a smaller unit gives a larger number of units.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Metric units are standardised
node.description: Metric units are standard units that allow measurements to be communicated and compared consistently.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Square units cover area
node.description: Area is measured by counting equal square units that cover a flat region.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Conversion scales the number
node.description: Converting units changes the numerical value according to the relative size of the units while preserving the quantity.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Estimate before measuring
node.description: Estimating before measuring supports unit choice and reasonableness checking.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare different attributes
node.description: Learner compares objects using different attributes, such as judging mass from height or capacity from width alone.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Bigger number always bigger measure
node.description: Learner assumes the larger number always means a larger measure without considering the unit size.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Gaps do not matter
node.description: Learner leaves gaps or overlaps between units and still treats the count as accurate.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Unit label without quantity
node.description: Learner gives a number without a unit or uses a unit label without connecting it to the measured attribute.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Convert by changing label only
node.description: Learner changes the unit label during conversion without scaling the numerical value.

edge.rationale: Choosing the attribute is central to direct comparison of measurable properties.
Direct length comparison is a core early measurement activity.
Mass comparison is a direct-comparison measurement case.
Capacity comparison is a direct-comparison measurement case.
Duration comparison applies direct comparison language to time intervals.
Unit iteration is the core action in informal measurement.
Avoiding gaps and overlaps is essential for accurate informal unit measurement.
Equal-sized units are foundational to meaningful measurement with units.
Counting units converts unit iteration into a numerical measure.
Choosing an appropriate informal unit supports efficient and meaningful measurement.
Length units are a central class of metric measurement units.
Mass units are common metric units in measurement contexts.
Capacity units are common metric units in liquid-volume contexts.
Time units are standard measurement units, though they are not metric in the same prefix structure as length, mass and capacity.
Square units extend metric unit ideas to area measurement.
Estimating with known units supports selecting and using metric units.
Metric prefixes and base units underpin metric unit conversions.
Length-unit conversion is a central unit-conversion case.
Mass and capacity conversions extend metric conversion across common attributes.
Area-unit conversion is a later and more complex application of unit conversion.
Reasonableness checking supports accurate unit conversion.
Attribute comparison builds on recognising quantities as comparable in some respect.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares objects globally without identifying the relevant measurable attribute.

edge.rationale: Direct length comparison requires selecting length, height or width as the attribute of interest.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares overall size rather than aligning a specific length dimension.

edge.rationale: Mass comparison requires focusing on heaviness rather than visual size.
edge.failure_signal: Learner assumes the taller or larger-looking object is heavier.

edge.rationale: Capacity comparison requires focusing on how much a container can hold.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares container height or width only without considering capacity.

edge.rationale: Duration comparison uses ordering and sequence language, though it develops alongside early time concepts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot compare which event lasted longer or shorter.

edge.rationale: Informal unit iteration builds on comparing and attending to a measurable attribute such as length.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places units without tracking the attribute being measured.

edge.rationale: Avoiding gaps and overlaps refines unit iteration for accuracy.
edge.failure_signal: Learner leaves spaces or stacks units but still counts them as accurate.

edge.rationale: Equal-sized unit reasoning follows from attending to how units are placed and counted.
edge.failure_signal: Learner mixes different unit sizes and treats the count as comparable.

edge.rationale: Counting units as a measure is only meaningful when the units are equal sized and consistently placed.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reports a count but cannot explain the unit or consistency of units.

edge.rationale: Choosing an informal unit depends on understanding that the unit count represents the measure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses a unit too large, too small or unrelated to the attribute.

edge.rationale: Metric length-unit selection builds on measuring length with consistent informal units.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses unrelated units or confuses length with area or mass.

edge.rationale: Selecting mass units builds on attending specifically to mass as the measured attribute.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses grams or kilograms based only on object size, not mass context.

edge.rationale: Selecting capacity units requires recognising capacity as the attribute being measured.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses length or mass units for capacity contexts.

edge.rationale: Selecting time units builds on comparing durations and time intervals.
edge.failure_signal: Learner selects units that are not appropriate for the duration scale.

edge.rationale: Square-unit area measurement extends equal-unit reasoning to covering surfaces.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts side lengths instead of square units covering the region.

edge.rationale: Estimating with metric units requires familiarity with common standard units and benchmarks.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives estimates with unreasonable units or scales.

edge.rationale: Metric prefixes and conversions depend on powers-of-ten scaling.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats centi, milli and kilo as labels without magnitude relationships.

edge.rationale: Length-unit conversions require knowing metric unit relationships and prefixes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner changes metres to centimetres without multiplying or dividing appropriately.

edge.rationale: Mass and capacity conversions require metric unit relationships for grams, kilograms, millilitres and litres.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses grams with litres or applies the wrong scale factor.

edge.rationale: Area-unit conversion requires understanding square units before scaling between them.
edge.failure_signal: Learner converts square units using a linear scale factor rather than an area scale factor.

edge.rationale: Reasonableness checking uses known conversion relationships to judge whether a result is plausible.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts converted values with impossible magnitude changes.
